2026-08-31.patch_summary: This patch introduces per-page_counter stock to improve the efficiency of memcg charge and limit checks. The current implementation uses per-cpu stocks, which can lead to expensive hierarchy walks and inefficient cache management. By pushing stock caches down to the page_counter level, each counter is responsible for its own charge, addressing issues such as limited cache capacity, per-CPU draining, and tight coupling with memcg. This change allows for more scalable and efficient handling of page counters.

reviews.author: Shakeel Butt
reviews.summary: Reviewer Shakeel Butt reported a compilation error on GCC 14.2.1 due to missing attribute before the __percpu pointer declaration, and suggested including an appropriate header.
reviews.raw_body:
On gcc 14.2.1, I get

In file included from mm/page_counter.c:8:
./include/linux/page_counter.h:47:44: error: expected \u2018:\u2019, \u2018,\u2019, \u2018;\u2019, \u2018}\u2019 or \u2018__attribute__\u2019 before \u2018*\u2019 token
   47 |         struct page_counter_stock __percpu *stock;
      |                                            ^

I think you need an appropriate header in this file.

2026-09-04.patch_summary: This patch introduces a per-page_counter stock to improve the performance of memcg charge and limit checks. The current implementation uses per-cpu stocks, which can lead to expensive hierarchy walks and inefficient cache management. By pushing stock caches down to the page_counter level, each counter is responsible for its own charge, reducing the need for CPU-wide draining and improving scalability when adding new page_counters to a memcg.
